_comment: Without water: rock with no aquifers, wet pockets, perched pools or springs (`Carvers.DRY`, which the hollows
an underground cuts answer to as well, so `dry rock` dries a great hall too), and on the whole Age the biomes
leaning dry and the sea leaning away. A cave under a sea still meets the sea, and the lava at the bottom stays.
It bars rock that is mostly water as well as drying what is left, so `dry flooded rock` is two words that cannot
both hold and is charged as the contradiction it is, where porous rock, wet only near the surface, dries.
Offered too, yielding to anything the book says: drier air, less rain.
Before the land, the ground or the air, it is the climate that is dry.
